title: Aviation Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) Planner (I) (LtCol to Capt) EMOS (7315, 7318), DC AVN
raw_text:
16. MOS 0588, Aviation Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) Planner
(I) (LtCol to Capt) EMOS (7315, 7318), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aviation Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO)
Planners plan, integrate, coordinate, supervise, de-conflict, and assess
actions principally by the Marine Corps and other aviation assess (but, also
by organic and non-organic systems operating in other domains) that exploit,
attack, and protect in and through the electromagnetic environment (EME) in
support of naval and fleet marine force objectives. Aviation EMSO Planners
advocate for and integrate air offensive, defensive, and EMSO support
capabilities in tactical and operational level plans, operations, and
activities in support of information. Operating primarily within the Marine
aircraft wing (MAW) and Marine division, Aviation EMSO Planners advise
commanders and staffs on the employment of aviation EMSO assets to
synchronize aspects of electromagnetic attack (EA), electromagnetic support
(ES), and electromagnetic protection (EP) in support of the commanders scheme
of maneuver. Aviation EMSO Planners maintain relationships with EMSO system
subject matter experts (SMEs), as well as joint and coalition capability SMEs
and planners. Aviation EMSO Planners are also represented within the service
headquarters and supporting establishment to support the development and
integration of EMSO capabilities into manned and unmanned aviation platforms
and operations.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Security requirement: must meet sensitive compartmented
information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a current single scope
background investigation (SSBI)/T5 investigation.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Must complete the Joint Electronic Warfare Theater Operations
Course (JEWTOC) (F16ABB5), Lackland AFB, San Antonio, TX.

        (2) Officers who have previously completed one of the following
courses are qualified to serve as a EW/UAS Officers MOS:

            (a) EA-6B Pilot Category I FRS Training Course (N26P3G4 or
M04P3GB) Whidbey Island, WA.

            (b) EA-6B ECMO Category I FRS Training Course (N26P4G4 or
M04P4GB) Whidbey Island, WA.

                (c) EA-6B Qualified Course (M04P3GB) MCAS Cherry Point, NC.


                                          1-42                       Enclosure (1)
 1108                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Waivers to any prerequisites or requirements must be submitted to
and approved by the occupational field 73 manager, HQMC DC Aviation.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Communications Officer, 0602.

            (2) Strategic Electromagnetic Spectrum Officer, 0640.

            (3) Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations Planner, 1704.

        (4) Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare/Cyberspace
Operations Officer, 2602.

            (5) Group 3 UAS MAGTF Officer, 7315.

            (6) VMU MQ-9 Officer, 7318.

            (7) Pilot, VMAQ EA-6B Qualified, 7543.

        (8) Naval Flight Officer (NFO) Qualified EA-6b Electronic Warfare
Officer, 7588.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
